note: The field of the place picture beyond the frame, as shares of the frame's width and height: left, right, bottom, top. Measured on the place picture itself (diag view beauty/picture at frames 2448 and 2706): the relief's apron is painted to the left and below as far as an eighth of the frame, to the right its outer layers end between 0.066 and 0.08 of the width beyond the frame, the sky above has no end.
pathNote: Mars flies the one move of the engine (plan E): one eye on one bell shaped rate from the hold to the surface view, drawn by both views, so at (the share of the segment at which the picture changes sides) moves nothing on the path. The sidestep of the dive, in radii in the frame of the camera that leaves the hold (right, up), is complete by the given share of the time of the segment. Phobos hangs 0.66 radii in front of the hold camera and 0.1 radii off its axis, low and to the right, and drifts right. Without a sidestep the eye passed 0.091 radii from its centre at frame 2415 and the moon swelled over the frame in 2411 to 2414. The lift of the older path (right -0.05, up 0.25, by 0.13) turned the camera by 0.165 of its mean from one frame to the next at 2403, twice the limit of the harness. With this one the eye steps left, the moon leaves by the right edge over frames 2406 to 2411 and the eye passes 0.237 radii from its centre at 2414; the turn changes by 0.072 of its mean at most. In 2410 and 2411 the flank of the moon at the edge of the frame is its stretched side.
riseNote: The rise is the one move too, from the surface view at its last pose to the first pose of the travel. It has an eye of its own: the plates of the globe are laid back from the eye of the dive at T (the twin of closePose) and are true from that eye only, so in the place window of the rise (frames 2688 to 2699 with at 0.237) the picture is seen from another eye and its sides show against the relief. That is cured by the close ground of plan F (both views in one frame, the border by distance on the ground), not by the path. at 0.861 and 0.15 put T on frames 2477 and 2681 (eye 0.00162 and 0.00129 radii up): the highest frames of each move in which the border of the close set is out of the frame (2475 and 2476 of the dive and 2683 to 2687 of the rise had it in the lower right corner).
edgeNote: edgeIn: left, right, bottom, top, as shares of the frame. While the picture's weight is under 1 its sides feather inward by this share times what is missing of the weight, so the picture comes in from the place outward and leaves toward it. Without it the right side of the picture stood as a straight slanted line against lighter ground in frames 2446 to 2449 and a pale wedge with a straight side at the upper right in 2444 to 2446. The top is less because the far field carries the horizon. Judged on every frame 2436 to 2459 and 2670 to 2744 at the draft tier: body colour steps into 2443 to 2454 between 0.92 and 3.45 (1.09 and 3.13 without).
limbNote: The close view has a bright band of dust haze on its horizon that the globe side does not draw. In the place window the camera is above the twin, so its limb lies beyond the horizon of the picture (8 pixels at frame 2447): the globe's dark sky and stars showed in that gap as a dark line under the haze. With limbReachDeg the sky of the picture is pushed down onto the limb of the camera, less and less up to that many degrees above it, and the ground the twin could not see takes the horizon row of the picture. At T nothing moves. Measured on frames 2444 to 2453 of the dive; the rise has the same eye.
